action: opened the order: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.

Untapped capability: proposed Unsaid (unsaid-widget, assumptions lifted from the thinking stream of turn.step), Pen (pen-widget, tool arguments drawn as they stream in), Attic (attic-widget, unused tools moved behind ToolSearch through tool.describe)

Person at the terminal: proposed Stamp (stamp-widget, how long you looked at each permission ask against how long it takes to read, from tool.check and PostToolUse duration_ms), Misdial (misdial-widget, holds a prompt whose files live in another open session's project), Gloss (gloss-widget, each flag of a command awaiting permission explained from the tool's own help)

Delight: proposed Palimpsest (palimpsest-widget, the words you typed and took back before sending, from prompt.edit against prompt.submit), Foregone (foregone-widget, the engine's own guess at your next prompt from the prompt.suggest event, sealed and scored against what you actually typed)
took the order at ideation

stamped reject on "Unsaid": Thinking chunks carry only what the person is shown live, which is summarised or absent on current models, and hedge keywords cannot tell an unchecked assumption from ordinary deliberation, so the card would be empty or wrong unless it pays for a model call every turn.

stamped reject on "Attic": Its cost is out of proportion: it saves a few thousand cached tokens of built-in tool schemas, which the engine already defers for MCP tools, at the price of silently changing which tools Claude reaches for.

stamped reject on "Stamp": Not chosen: the look time is inferred from tool.check resolving, which is not the dialog opening when asks queue or a mode's classifier decides, so its headline accusation can be false, and its 'make this a rule' half repeats guard-widget.

stamped reject on "Misdial": A variation on squiggle-widget joined to the sessions registry: squiggle already marks the missing file names as you type, and prompts that spell out full paths meant for another window are too rare to carry a widget.

stamped reject on "Gloss": Its cost is out of proportion to what it gives: help text formats differ per tool and subcommand and there is no man on Windows, so the parser would mostly say 'no help found' or wrongly flag real flags as invented.

stamped reject on "Palimpsest": Not chosen: it is new and it works, but it is a moment of amusement that changes nothing about the work, and telling a retracted thought from a fixed typo without a model is guesswork.

stamped reject on "Foregone": A variation on wager-widget's prediction scoring with the roles swapped; one similarity figure that is mentioned once and then ignored, and it is blank whenever suggestions do not show.
named the widget pen-widget ("Pen")

stamped pass: Pen is the only idea that is both new and certain to work: it reads the tool-argument chunks of turn.step, which no widget touches, at no token cost, and moves the person's chance to stop a bad write from after it ran to while it is being written.

For the director (spec note 10): the demo stand-in needs docs/engine.js to run generator hooks and dispatch a turn.step stream of tool and input chunks before each scripted Write, Edit and Bash call; that file is outside the widget folder and is not changed, so until it lands the demo card shows the empty sentence.

Live run not made (spec note 11): the machinist may not start claude sessions, so the piece count p is unmeasured and whether arguments arrive in pieces on this engine is unproven; render.ts dispatches no turn.step, so only the empty state was looked at there and the other states rest on the exact rows asserted in A3, A7, A8 and A13.

Found while building: every state get of one dispatch reads one moment, so a switch-off made mid-step was invisible to the step and one copy landed after it; copies are now written with ifVersion and the switch's version is compared after a miss, which also keeps an off-then-on inside one step silent (A14).

stamped pass: Built pen-widget: a turn.step stream hook with an incremental JSON reader that draws the tail of the Write, Edit, NotebookEdit, Bash or PowerShell call being written, with 14 acceptance tests and the checker passing.
